draft.title: The atmosphere
card: The atmosphere is the layer of gases held around the Earth by gravity. It is mostly nitrogen, about 78%, and oxygen, about 21%, with small amounts of other gases such as carbon dioxide and water vapour.

Weather happens in the lowest layer, the troposphere, where most of the air and water vapour is found. Weather is the state of the air at a place and time. Climate is the pattern of weather over many years.
The greenhouse effect keeps the planet warm. Gases such as carbon dioxide, methane and water vapour absorb some of the heat the Earth gives off and send part of it back towards the surface.
Without the natural greenhouse effect, the Earth would be much colder. Extra greenhouse gases from human activity strengthen the effect and can warm the planet further.
draft.remember: The atmosphere is the gas layer where weather happens, and its greenhouse gases keep the Earth warm.

a.q: Which statement best explains how the greenhouse effect keeps the Earth warm?
opts: Some gases absorb heat from the Earth and return part of it
Some gases trap sunlight so it cannot reach the ground
Some gases thicken the air so the Sun gives off more heat
Some gases block the wind so warm air cannot move away
a.why: Greenhouse gases absorb heat given off by the Earth and send part of it back towards the surface, which keeps the lower atmosphere warmer. They do not stop sunlight reaching the ground, and they do not make the Sun give off more heat.
a.clue: Think about heat leaving the Earth, not sunlight arriving.

b.q: A student says, "Sydney had a cold, wet week, so the climate must be cooling." What is wrong with this claim?
opts: One week of weather is not a pattern over many years
Weather and climate are the same thing, so it is correct
Weather in the troposphere cannot affect a city's climate
A wet week shows the greenhouse effect has stopped working
b.why: Climate is the pattern of weather over many years, so one cold, wet week says little about it. The tempting option says weather and climate are the same, but the card separates a short-term state from a long-term pattern.
b.clue: Compare how long weather and climate are measured over.
